_comment: Card ownership, granted by the controller. launch_gate reads launch_block_granted
and note; a false grant with no note reads as a stub, not as a decision.
Idle is not free: a card's owner is the job still running or the one the controller
has queued, never the instantaneous nvidia-smi row.
AND A STALE GRANT IS WORSE THAN NO GRANT (b0 2026-09-03): the 0-7 grant below outlived
the run it was made for, so the next launcher would have read it as licence to take
cards 4 and 7 -- which hold the USER'S OWN work in another container. The rule above
cuts both ways: a card's owner is not the nvidia-smi row, and it is not a superseded

lane_two_card_exception: GRANTED 2026-09-03, narrow, one job: de's dist.all_to_all_single microbench may hold BOTH lane cards at once. The 05:39Z widening was three jobs one card each and de read it correctly as not covering this. The exception is not 'big jobs may take two': it is that MEASURING A LINK REQUIRES TWO ENDPOINTS -- a two-rank all_to_all on one card is a device-to-device copy and measures nothing about NVLink, so there is no one-card version of this job to fall back to. Bounded by occupancy, not by importance: 110 MB x ~10 repeats is SECONDS. Any job that structurally needs two endpoints AND occupies seconds qualifies; a job that merely runs faster on two cards does not.
